newIssues.record_or_file: flywheel-shooter, dual-flywheel-shooter, hooded-flywheel, kicker-wheel, roller-ejector (preset) and ui/sim-mechanism-list.js add()
newIssues.evidence: These records use continuous joint types (flywheel, feeder, roller-intake). Their presets are {states:{stop:0,run:1},speed:1}; roller-ejector has run:-1. For continuous types a state is a position in degrees (sim-mechanism-types.js: 'a "run" position (a few turns)'). The type defaults are run:3600 at speed 18000 (flywheel), run:3600 at speed 3600 (feeder) and run:2160 at speed 2400 (roller-intake). add() copies p.states and p.speed onto the joint and the actuator, so Add to robot makes a part whose 'run' action turns 1 degree at 1 deg/s. kicker-wheel (feeder) is not in AS_GAME, so this happens even with BIOBUZZ on. The other four go through it only when the game is off.
newIssues.fix: Delete preset from these 5 records, or set it in the type's units: flywheel {states:{stop:0,run:3600},speed:18000}, feeder {states:{stop:0,run:3600},speed:3600}, roller-ejector {states:{stop:0,run:-2160},speed:2400}. Add a test that a preset's states are the same order of magnitude as the type default for continuous joints.

newIssues.evidence: how: 'Output speed and force vary with angle and are highest when the bars are perpendicular'. For a fixed input, output force times speed equals the input power, so force is lowest where speed is highest. A slider-crank's force is highest near the toggle (dead-center) positions, which the record's own 'past center the linkage locks' depends on.
newIssues.fix: how: '...Output speed is highest near the middle of the stroke, where the crank and link are near perpendicular. Output force is highest near the ends of the stroke, close to the toggle positions. Past center the linkage locks against backdriving...'

newIssues.record_or_file: deployable-intake, claw-family, camera-pan, camera-pan-tilt, pan-tilt-platform, wrist-mounted-camera (preset.states)
newIssues.evidence: deploy-intake is positive:'lower' with default {up:0,down:90}, and the child biobuzz-ramp-intake follows that ({up:0,down:100}). deployable-intake has {up:90,down:0}, so the 'up' route action swings it 90 degrees toward the floor. camera-mount's default down:20 means positive is down, but camera-pan, camera-pan-tilt and pan-tilt-platform use down:-30, and wrist-mounted-camera uses down:-90. Every claw record uses {open:35,closed:0}, while the claw type default is {open:0,closed:25}.
newIssues.fix: deployable-intake preset.states: {up:0,down:90}. Camera presets: down:+30 (wrist-mounted-camera: {up:0,down:90}). Either switch the claw presets to {open:0,closed:N} like the type, or document that the claw's CAD pose is closed.

newIssues.record_or_file: telescoping-intake, extendo (params and preset; both rule-checked R105)
newIssues.evidence: BIOBUZZ R105 limits a robot to 18 x 24 in. after the start, so a horizontal slide on an 18 in. robot can reach only about 6 in. beyond the frame. telescoping-intake defaults extension to 12 in. (max 24), with preset out:12 and upper:18. extendo defaults to 450 mm (17.7 in.), with preset out:18 and upper:22. Both are marked rule-checked against R105, but the numbers they ship with break R105 on a typical BIOBUZZ robot.
newIssues.fix: telescoping-intake: extension default 5, max 6 in., note 'BIOBUZZ R105: 24 in. total length, so about 6 in. beyond an 18 in. frame'; preset {states:{in:0,out:5},upper:6}. extendo: extension default 150 mm, note the same; preset {states:{in:0,out:5},upper:6}. Or keep the bigger values only as historical (INTO THE DEEP) and say so in the note.
